environment.runtime: Node v26.7.0 under vitest 5, forks pool

method.budget: 200 ms is the longest main-thread stall a worker-failure rescue may cost. Above it the honest answer is a refusal that says nothing was produced, not a frozen page.
method.terrain: computeTerrainCore over the deterministic bench cloud in tests/helpers/terrainBenchCloud.ts (a 1000 m span of rolling terrain). Best of 3 runs per row. Ladder A moves the point count at a fixed 40 m cell (625 cells); ladder B moves the cell size over a fixed 2 000-point cloud; ladder C times the candidate limit pairs together.
method.classify: deriveClassification over the same bench cloud, default options, best of 3 runs per row.
method.proxy: These are Node timings. Node and a browser tab run the same V8 on different heaps and under different scheduling, so the numbers stand as a proxy for the browser main thread, not as a measurement of it. Read a crossing point as an order of magnitude.
method.shape: Terrain cost is driven by grid cells more than by points: a sparse cloud over a fine grid spends nearly all of its time filling voids (2 000 points over 250 000 cells measured 48 s in the same harness). That is why the terrain guard bounds both terms.

terrainMaxFallbackPoints.basis: The corner row 25 000 points over 1 024 cells measures 198.8 ms, inside the budget; 50 000 over the same grid measures 223.4 ms and is outside it.

terrainMaxFallbackCells.basis: The cell ladder crosses the budget at 1 024 cells (194.6 ms at 2 000 points, 224.8 ms at 1 600 cells), so the shipped bound sits just under the last row inside the budget.

classifyMaxFallbackPoints.basis: 132.9 ms at 1 000 000 points, 266.5 ms at 2 000 000, so the crossing lies between the two and the shipped bound is the last row inside the budget.
